name: wavvy 3.5in ILI9488 panel (plain ESP32 WROOM)
summary: Electrically identical to the 4.0in board and differs in exactly one field: it is not stable at 80MHz.

render.reason: Same geometry and same arithmetic as the 4.0in board: 320x480 at 8 bits indexed is 153.6KB in one block, which the ESP32 will not give you with WiFi up, so the compositor works in 16-row bands. The halved clock costs roughly 3 fps on top, blit 35ms to 53ms for a 320x192 draw, which does not change the buffer strategy.

display.pixel_format_reason: The ILI9488 has no 16-bit SPI pixel mode. Every pixel is three bytes on the wire, using the top 6 bits of each channel. That is the hard ceiling on frame rate.
display.clock_reason: Measured, and the single most expensive fact in this registry. THIS BOARD IS NOT STABLE AT 80MHz. It renders structured block corruption: squares, lines, smearing, because whole bytes are lost mid-block rather than bits flipped at random. 40MHz fixes it at the cost of about 3 fps. The panel IS an ILI9488, same as the 4.0in board, verified with a labelled test card after the corruption pattern initially looked like an ST7796 being driven with 3-byte pixels. Do not raise this clock, and do not re-diagnose the corruption as a wrong-driver problem.

bluetooth_keyboard.reason: No touch and no panel-side buttons, so a BLE keyboard is the only real input. NimBLE at 19KB rather than Bluedroid at 83KB, same as every other no-PSRAM board in the fleet.

touch.absent_reason: Bare panel module wired to a plain ESP32 devkit. There is no touch layer on the glass and no touch controller on either board.

bad_baud_rates.reason: Invalid head of packet (0xFF) on this CP2102 cable, including for plain esptool reads. It is the cable, not the board.
Same Invalid head of packet (0xFF) failure as 921600.

panel_id_register.note: Same read, same garbage, same conclusion as the 4.0in board: 0xD3 returns 00 7F DF, matching no known part. Identity comes from this file and a human, not from the panel.

distinguishing_notes: 3.5 inch panel. That is the only difference from the 4.0in board: same chip, same flash, same controller, same wiring, same clone CP2102 reporting USB serial 0001.
If a board renders blocks, lines and static rather than a picture, it is this board running the 4.0in profile at 80MHz.
locationID in ioreg -r -c IOUSBHostDevice -l is unique per physical USB port and can tell two identical bridges apart if both are plugged in.
identification.confirm_prompt: Is this the 3.5 inch panel? It is the slower of the two identical-looking boards: 40MHz, not 80MHz. Getting this wrong gives structured block corruption that looks like a dead panel.

gotchas.text: 40MHz, not 80MHz. At 80MHz this specific module renders blocks, lines and static. The corruption is structured rather than speckled because whole bytes are lost mid-block, which is what tells you it is a clock problem and not a driver problem. The panel is an ILI9488 and that was verified visually; do not go looking for an ST7796.
No 16-bit SPI pixel mode. Three bytes per pixel, always. A full 320x480 frame is 460.8KB on the wire.
230400 only. 921600 and 460800 both fail with Invalid head of packet (0xFF) on this CP2102 cable, including for esptool reads.

MISO is deliberately left unassigned even though GPIO19 is available. The panel is write-only, and the ESP32 SPI driver refuses to clock above 26.7MHz once a MISO pin is bound. On this board that would drop the clock below the 40MHz it needs.
153.6KB of indexed framebuffer will not come back as one contiguous allocation with WiFi up. Band rendering is the only thing that fits.
Attaching a serial monitor resets the board through DTR/RTS. Anything streaming to it drops for a few seconds and reconnects.
Both CP2102 bridges in the fleet report USB serial 0001, so with both boards plugged in the /dev/cu.usbserial-* names collide. Flash one at a time, or match on locationID from ioreg.
